q: What is Wen Counter?
bold: A free till in a web page.
f: Wen Counter, opened by the Wen Open Lab on November 12, 2026, is a till that lives in a web page: type the amount, show a Solana Pay QR, and the chain confirms the sale. No server, no app store, no card data, no fee per sale.

q: How much can a card fee take from a 3-dollar coffee?
f: On a 3-dollar coffee a published plan of 2.9% + 30¢ takes 12.9%, because the fixed part of the fee hurts small tickets most. With Wen Counter the till costs 0; the buyer's wallet pays only the Solana network fee, 5,000 lamports per signature.

q: Which requests is Wen Counter allowed to send?
f: The counter never connects to a wallet, never asks it to sign and holds no key. Its code may send only getSignaturesForAddress, getTransaction and getAccountInfo, so there is no path from the counter to the shop's money.

q: What does the Wen Counter ledger show?
bold: The card fee you did not pay.
f: The ledger measures the card fee you did not pay from confirmed sales at your card terms, shows the effective rate of your own ticket mix, and exports a CSV for your accountant for today, a week, a month, a quarter, a year or any period.

q: Who decides which wallet a Wen Counter pays into?
bold: Only the owner, behind a PIN.
f: Setup is locked by a PIN, so nobody at the till can put their own wallet in. Forgot it? Reinstall, enter the wallets again and set a new PIN: nothing on-chain changes, and every QR shows the address, so a swap cannot stay hidden.

q: Can one Wen Counter serve several departments?
f: Wallet #1 plus wallets #2..X, each with a type and a name, such as #2 · Department · Toys or #3 · Tips · Bar tips. The cashier picks where the sale goes, and the head office view adds up sales per wallet.

q: How many open checks guard Wen Counter?
f: 25 checks for the logic, 13 that prove by reading the code that the counter cannot sign, send or reach a wallet, and 19 in a real phone browser with fake wallets, hostile text, the setup PIN and the head office view. Anyone can rerun them.

q: What does Wen ask in return for Wen Counter?
f: "We require nothing," Wen says: post on X or on your site that you use the WEN solution, with its name, and nobody will ever ask how many shops you run.

q: When does Wen Counter count a payment as paid?
f: A payment counts only when the reference, the recipient, the token, the amount and the success all match on-chain. Anything else stays unpaid.

q: How is the original Wen Counter build recognised?
f: One WCP-1 block fingerprint identifies the original build of the counter, so a copy can be checked against it; the code and the 57 checks are public for anyone to rerun.

q: How does a shop refund a Wen Counter sale?
bold: With a new payment, marked refund.
f: A refund is a new payment from the shop's own wallet, with refund: plus the original transaction in the memo, so anyone can match the two.

q: How many steps does it take to open your own Wen Counter?
f: Open the counter on a phone or tablet, create a wallet in a Solana wallet app you trust, register it in Setup behind your own PIN, paste the receiving address (the counter checks it on-chain), and manage the money in your own wallet.

q: Is a Wen Counter receipt a fiscal receipt?
f: The buyer can get a QR, the text or a receipt NFT, but it is not a fiscal receipt: shops check their country's rules and talk to their accountant.

q: What can a cashier attach to a Wen Counter sale?
f: A comment, such as a product code or a name, lands in the ledger, the receipt and the CSV, and travels with the payment as a memo where the buyer's wallet supports it. A memo is public.

q: How much did US merchants pay in card fees in 2024?
f: US merchants paid $187.2 billion in card fees in 2024, and shops pay roughly 1–3% on every card sale. Small tickets, like skewers at a street grill, feel the fixed part of the fee most.

q: How long did a devnet sale take on Wen Counter?
f: The almanac's devnet video shows a sale going from the QR to ✓ Paid in 17 seconds, with the QR blurred on purpose.

q: Who is Wen Counter made for first?
bold: Crypto communities, events and online shops.
f: The solution names its audience honestly: crypto communities, events and online shops for their own audience, not mass adoption. Seven answers to read before scaling are written down on the solution page.

q: How can a chain of shops close the day with Wen Counter?
bold: By moving the takings to the company wallet.
f: For a chain: a till wallet per branch, and in the evening the day's takings move to the company wallet, for example a multisig.

q: Who controls the money when a shop uses Wen Counter?
bold: The shop, in its own wallet.
f: The mechanism takes nothing, holds nothing and charges nothing; it follows the Solana network's rules, and the wallet is the shop's own. The shop uses the solution on its own responsibility.

q: What is the first Wen Counter setup PIN?
f: The first PIN is a deployment parameter, a simple 1111, and the owner changes it at the first start so nobody at the till can change the wallets.

q: What does the Wen Open Lab build?
f: The Lab takes the open tools behind Wen, the WNS token layout, Solana Token-2022 and Solana Pay, and builds free, working models that a developer, a shop, a fintech team or a bank can study, test and reuse.

q: How does a Wen Open Lab receipt keep an order private?
f: The shop hashes the order (id, product, price, date) with SHA-256; only the hash goes on-chain, in a Token-2022 mint with its metadata inside the token and a supply locked at exactly one.

q: What happens if a WNS royalty hook's conditions are not met?
bold: The whole transfer is rolled back.
f: A WNS NFT carries the Token-2022 Transfer Hook extension naming the royalty program diste3nXmK7ddDTs1zb6uday6j4etCa9RChD8fJ1xay. Token-2022 calls it on every transfer, and if its conditions are not met the whole transaction is rolled back.

q: What does the Lab's B2B settlement token refuse?
f: The Stage 3 model builds a settlement token that refuses payments carrying no invoice memo and refuses counterparties nobody approved: business rules inside the token itself.

q: How fast is a payment final in the Lab's Solana Pay bridge?
f: The Payments Bridge confirms a Solana Pay payment in seconds and treats it as final in about 13 seconds, where card acquiring authorizes in seconds but settles the money in days.
